scope: Only the benchmark calendar/provenance delta and its retained focused regressions. No original execution, framework/binary modification or criterion change.
reviewedBoundaries: scenarioBody selects native content_item_kinds aligned with content items and the current turn_id; top-level and native metadata turn IDs must match. Historical turns and user examples are left unchanged.

The same-turn native application carrier must match the previously acknowledged formatter hash, calendar-state hash and generation. Its YYYY-MM-DD date is checked using the same IANA timezone and ticking scenario offset; the environment timezone must agree.

The only additional calendar mutation is the selected environment current_date text. Existing model/effort binding is separately preserved. Body metadata, create_time, user content, OS/auth/TLS and monotonic deadlines are not rewritten.

The native proxy passes its original decoded JSON bytes into the common preparation seam used by HTTP and WebSocket. Private O_EXCL/0600/fsync artifacts retain those original bytes, the body after existing native/model preparation but before calendar binding, and the outgoing JSON body. These are application JSON bytes, not headers or compressed HTTP wire bytes.

Missing or ambiguous current carriers, mismatched turn/timezone, stale generation or absent original bytes refuse preparation before a permit. Helper requests take the same strict calendar path; unsupported helper carrier shapes stop rather than inheriting a guessed date.

Both physical transport boundaries now recheck the existing ledger/deadline after synchronous retention and the final save. The dispatched flag is set only after this last check, immediately before the transport call. A retained permit without dispatch remains usage-unknown under the existing accounting policy.
